**B85. The type-check task reports every file it did not check as IMPROVED, so a narrowed run claims 296 improvements of which 296 are false.** Added 2026-11-02T18:01:38+00:00. **WHAT THIS IS, in plain terms.** `scripts/type_check_task_2026-11-01.py` keeps a per-file baseline and reports any file whose finding count has fallen as IMPROVED, inviting `--update` to lock the gain in. Its `--paths` flag narrows the run to named files. **The 2 features interact wrongly: an unchecked file returns 0 findings, and 0 against a non-zero baseline reads as a complete improvement.** **MEASURED BY RUNNING IT BOTH WAYS, which is the only way this could be seen.** A full run reports **0** improvements. The same task with `--paths scripts/suite_record.py` reports **296**. All 296 are files the narrowed run never opened: **296 of 296 false, 1.000000, Wilson 95% [0.987188, 1.000000], Clopper-Pearson [0.987615, 1.000000]**. **WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC.** The report's next instruction is to run `--update` to lock the improvement in. Doing so after a narrowed run would write 0 as the new baseline for 295 files that were never examined, **silently ratcheting the whole project to a number nothing measured** — and the ratchet would then refuse every later commit that merely restored the true count. The failure direction is the dangerous one: it makes the instrument look like it is winning. **IT IS AN INSTANCE OF A RULE THE PROJECT ALREADY WROTE DOWN.** *Compare lint counts like with like*, recorded 2026-10-15 after a path-sensitive linter produced a spurious `+1` that led to good prose being deleted to satisfy it. The same shape, in a different instrument, 18 days later. **HOW IT WAS FOUND, and it was nearly believed.** Running the task on 1 file while fixing the single risen entry printed *"IMPROVED, 275 file(s)"*, and that figure was about to be read as 275 real improvements from the day's work. It was caught by asking what population the 296 was drawn from. **RECOMMENDATION. Simplest sufficient:** when the run is narrowed, compare only the files actually checked, and say so in the output — the improved and unbaselined sections should be computed over the checked set, not over the whole baseline. **Additive:** no capability is lost; `--paths` keeps working and the full run is unchanged. What is removed is the ability to report an improvement in a file that was not examined, which is not a capability. **A guard must not need a live defect:** the regression test should run the task narrowed and full over a fixture baseline and assert that the narrowed run reports 0 improvements outside its own path set, so it has subjects whether or not the live tree currently misreports. **No composability claim.** **THE TASK IS OTHERWISE SOUND AND WAS RUN TO COMPLETION, which is its own entry's business:** 757 files checked, **1,133 findings about this project across 296 files, 0.391017 of files affected, Wilson [0.356889, 0.426246]**, a mean of 3.827703 per affected file, and 1,273 third-party stub errors across 551 files which it reports and deliberately never ratchets. **1 file had RISEN against its baseline and was FIXED rather than baselined away** — `scripts/suite_record.py`, where a float and a `list[str]` were being assigned into a mapping inferred as `dict[str, int]`; both were real, the counters are now annotated `int` so the arithmetic stays checked, and the widening happens at 1 visible point. `Any` was deliberately not used, because it would make the checker pass by refusing to look. ★ **B85 IS FIXED AND GUARDED, 2026-11-02T18:05:25+00:00, AND THE REPAIR IS CONFINEMENT RATHER THAN A NEW FEATURE.** **WHAT CHANGED.** Every baseline comparison is now computed over `checked` — the files the run actually opened, decided by `_was_checked`, which accepts an exact path or a file under a checked directory — and `--update` MERGES into the existing baseline instead of replacing it. **A full run behaves exactly as before**, because then `checked` is every file. **THE SECOND DEFECT, FOUND WHILE READING THE FIRST, WAS THE WORSE ONE.** `--update` assigned `led["files"] = proj`, which REPLACED the whole baseline. So a narrowed update would not merely have written an optimistic 0 — it would have **DELETED every unchecked file's entry**, and all 295 of them would have returned as unbaselined on the next run, refusing every commit until re-baselined. The report's own next line is an instruction to run `--update`, so the path from the false report to the damage was 1 step. **PROVEN BY EXECUTION, WITH THE ANTI-VACUITY HALF THAT MATTERS.** `scripts/the_type_check_confinement_mutations_2026-11-02.py` raises a victim file's baseline so a naive comparison would call it improved, then checks 3 properties: **M1** a narrowed run stays SILENT about it; **M2** a FULL run still REPORTS it as improved; **M3** a narrowed `--update` KEEPS the entries it did not check. **3 of 3 hold.** **M2 is the one that makes M1 mean anything** — without it, a task that reported no improvements at all would satisfy M1, and the capability would have been removed rather than corrected, which is the failure the additive standard names. The harness copies the ledger byte-for-byte before touching it and verifies the sha256 matches after; the restoration was confirmed identical. **THE GUARD GOES RED ON EACH HALF OF THE REPAIR: 3 of 3 reversions red** — the improved comparison unconfined, the update replacing instead of merging, and the prefix check losing its directory boundary so that `scripts_old/a.py` would read as inside `scripts`. That third one is the substring-match error this project has recorded more often than any other, most recently when `bound` matched `severity_bounds_validation`. The source was restored byte-for-byte and the guard passes again. **IT DOES NOT NEED A LIVE DEFECT.** All 10 tests build their own ledger and file set, so the properties are exercised whether or not the live tree currently misreports anything. **AGAINST THE 3 STANDARDS. Simplest sufficient:** 1 predicate and 2 gated comparisons; no new file format, no new flag, no change to a full run. **Additive:** `--paths` keeps working, the full run is unchanged, and what is removed is the ability to report an improvement in a file that was not examined — not a capability. **No composability claim:** the confinement alone is sufficient, and the 2 edits are 2 halves of 1 fix rather than 2 fixes composed.

**B86. The markdown-companion rebuilder matched a TYPED note-standard version, so the v1.9 bump broke it on the current report while it still worked on yesterday's.** Added 2026-11-02T18:08:42+00:00. **STATUS: FIXED, VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, AND A SECOND CLAIM OF MINE WITHDRAWN IN THE SAME PASS.** **WHAT THIS IS.** `scripts/rebuild_morning_report_markdown_2026-10-30.py` carried `FOOT_PREFIX = "Written under CDSFL note standard v1.8"` and raises a `ValueError` when no line starts with it, because a report without its foot line cannot be rebuilt faithfully. The note standard was bumped to **v1.9 on 2026-11-01** on his own instruction, so every report written since is stamped v1.9. **MEASURED BY EXECUTION RATHER THAN BY READING: the v1.8 prefix matches 1 foot line in `Morning_Report_2026-11-01.txt` and 0 in `Morning_Report_2026-11-02_GENERATED.txt`.** So the rebuilder would have raised on the current report while working on the previous one — a breakage introduced by a correct change elsewhere, which is why no test caught it. **THE FOLLOW FOUND EXACTLY 1 LIVE INSTANCE, which is worth stating because the grep hit 40-odd lines.** Searching every typed note-standard version across `scripts/`, `bench/` and `hooks/` returns matches that are overwhelmingly either historical WRITERS — a script correctly stamping the standard in force when it was written — or test fixtures that are deliberately typed, or guards asserting the current standard, which is their job. **Only this 1 is a MATCHER**, and a version typed into a matcher is the same shape as the stale counts this project keeps finding. **THE FIX IS TO MATCH ANY DECLARED VERSION**, which is strictly MORE permissive: every archival stamp from v1.3 onward still matches, so no historical report stops being readable. Verified after the change: **1 foot line matched in BOTH reports.** **THE PROJECT'S CANONICAL FOOT-LINE RULE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT COPIED HERE.** `declared_version` in `bench/tests/test_note_standard_v17_enforced_2026-08-26.py` holds a note to the HIGHEST version on any foot-line-shaped line and ignores prose mentions — a rule adopted on 2026-09-17 after the first version silently exempted notes that quoted an older standard in their prose. That rule exists to decide which RULES a note is held to. This script only needs to LOCATE the foot line so it can be preserved, so a prefix match is the simplest sufficient predicate, and copying the stricter rule here would create a second place for it to drift. **A SECOND CLAIM OF MINE IS WITHDRAWN, AND THIS IS THE USEFUL HALF.** Running the rebuilder end-to-end against today's date raised `FileNotFoundError` on `Morning_Report_2026-11-02.txt`, and I took that for a seam defect: the generator writes `Morning_Report_<date>_GENERATED.txt` while the rebuilder looks for `Morning_Report_<date>.txt`, and 9 of the 28 archived morning reports carry the `_GENERATED` suffix. **IT IS NOT A DEFECT.** `scripts/morning_report_build_2026-10-12.py` writes BOTH the spoken `.txt` and the markdown companion `.md` for a generated report — `experimental_notes/Morning_Report_2026-11-02_GENERATED.md` exists at 25,902 bytes — so a generated report needs no rebuild. The rebuilder exists for the HAND-WRITTEN reports, which is what its own docstring says: a hand fix to `Morning_Report_2026-10-30.md` came back on the next rebuild. **A `FileNotFoundError` on a generated date is correct behaviour, and repairing it would have made the rebuilder fight the generator for ownership of the same file.** **AGAINST THE 3 STANDARDS. Simplest sufficient:** 1 string shortened. **Additive:** the matcher accepts strictly more than before and nothing is removed. **No composability claim.** 80 guards across the 3 note-standard and companion test files pass after the change.

The severity specification asks for a quantity the operational directive rules inadmissible, and the HARD/SOFT classification it also needs is instructed on every finding with nowhere to record it.** Added 2026-11-02T20:26:35+00:00. **FOUND BY THE COMPACTION-BOUNDARY RE-CHECK, not by reading the specification.** Re-running the producers behind the preceding commit moved 1 figure, and following it reached this. **WHAT SECTION 7.7 ASKS FOR.** `docs/MATHEMATICAL_APPENDIX.md` section 7.7 states `Sev(f) = W(class) . confidence . V(verification)`, with the key property that a disproved finding scores 0 regardless of confidence. **3 factors. V IS COLLECTED** — it is the harness's own falsifier verdict. **THE OTHER 2 ARE NOT, AND FOR OPPOSITE REASONS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE FINDING.** **(1) `confidence` IS REFUSED BY POLICY, NOT MISSING BY OVERSIGHT.** `bench/directives/universal/cdsfl_operational.md` carries a gate named `d_tool` whose words are: *"The detection probability d entering q = eta . d . p must come from actual tool execution (static analysis, test runner, SymPy verification, AST parse), not from self-assessed confidence. A claim of d = 0.9 based on \"I am certain\" is not admissible. d = 0.9 derived from \"9 of 10 relevant tests caught the flaw class\" is admissible. Formally: d_i = f(T_i) where T_i is the result of executing a defined verification tool."* And again, under the admissibility gates, quoted with its line wrapping normalised and nothing else changed, because the source breaks it across 3 lines with 3-space indents: *"Self-reported confidence is not accepted. Assertions that \"my reasoning is sound\" without tool receipts are inadmissible under this directive."* **THE OTHER 5 QUOTATIONS IN THIS ENTRY ARE BYTE-EXACT LIFTS, VERIFIED BY SEARCHING THE FILE FOR EACH ONE BEFORE IT WAS WRITTEN HERE — 5 of 6 matched as written and this 1 did not, which is why it is labelled rather than presented as verbatim. **MEASURED: `confidence` appears on 0 of 3,311 archived findings, Wilson 95% [0.000000, 0.001159], Clopper-Pearson [0.000000, 0.001114] — and that is the directive working as designed rather than a gap.** **(2) THE HARD/SOFT CLASS IS THE OPPOSITE: REQUIRED AND HOMELESS.** Section 11 of the same directive reads *"Before producing any output, classify every constraint as HARD or SOFT. HARD: physics, mathematics, law, safety, explicit absolutes. Non-negotiable. SOFT: economic, preference, convenience. Negotiable."* **MEASURED: of 98 distinct fields across those 3,311 findings, 0 hold a HARD/SOFT class.** The only candidates are `flaw_class`, present on 3,311 of 3,311 and recorded in the shadow's own docstring as *"section 4's integer class id, a different quantity"*, and `withdraw_reason` on 50. **So an instruction given to every model before it produces anything has no field to land in.** **WHY THIS IS A DECISION AND NOT A BUILD.** The specification cannot be implemented as written without accepting self-reported confidence, and the directive forbids exactly that. **So the shadow's substitution of the asserted severity for `W . confidence` is not a shortcut — it is the only admissible route that currently exists**, which reframes the answer to the severity question he has asked 3 times. **THE 3 OPTIONS, AND ALL 3 ARE HIS.** **(a) AMEND SECTION 7.7** so its 2nd factor is tool-derived rather than self-assessed — the form the `d_tool` gate already prescribes. **(b) NARROW THE DIRECTIVE'S REFUSAL** to permit a confidence that is itself a function of tool output, which is arguably what `d_tool` already licenses and would make the formula implementable unchanged. **(c) ADOPT THE SHADOW'S SUBSTITUTION FORMALLY** — the asserted severity stands in for `W . confidence`, V applies alone — and record that section 7.7 is implemented in that reduced form rather than as written. **RECOMMENDATION: (b), because it is the smallest change that leaves both documents true.** `d_tool` already draws the line at *self-assessed* rather than at confidence as such, and a confidence derived from tool receipts satisfies it; (a) edits the mathematics to fit a parsing accident, and (c) leaves the appendix stating a formula nothing implements. **ADDING THE HARD/SOFT FIELD IS SEPARABLE AND IS NOT A DECISION:** the directive already requires the classification, so recording it is carrying out an instruction rather than changing one. **NEEDS HIS RULING:** which of (a), (b) or (c) governs section 7.7's 2nd factor. The facility was never pointed at a target it could act on, so saying it never worked is true and says less than it appears to. **ESTABLISHED BY CALLING `_apply_back_gate`, NOT BY READING IT**, per `execute-do-not-grep`: the prose target's OWN bytes, prose sharing no sentence with it, and `bench/runner_core.py` fed its own bytes all drew the SAME refusal. A no-op cannot break a test, so the verdict did not depend on its input, and because the third case is Python the fault was never confined to prose. **WHAT `_apply_back_gate` DOES, AND WHERE THE 3 FAILURES COME FROM.** It copies the repository into a sandbox with `.git`, `bench/logs` and the credentials excluded, overlays the candidate, runs the configured suite and rejects on any non-zero exit. It never ran that suite WITHOUT the candidate, so it had no baseline. The 3 failures were `TestCounterfactual` in `bench/tests/test_immune_memory_evaluation.py`, whose `_all_archived_decisions()` globs `bench/logs` at line 101 of that file -- the directory the copy deliberately omits. The same suite is GREEN in the repository: 73 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed. The sandbox turns 22 of those passes into skips and 3 into failures. **AND THE PROSE HALF IS A RECURRENCE, NOT A NEW FAULT.** The honest refusal for a non-Python target sat INSIDE `if not test_cmd:`, so it spoke only when no command was configured; a prose target WITH one fell through to pytest. z3 on the branch structure returns `unsat` for the conjunction that would reach it, and SymPy's `simplify_logic` independently returns `False`. `bench/tools/commissioning_arms_2026-09-21.py` had already fixed this on 2026-09-30 for its own prose arm by passing an EMPTY `--test-cmd`, and its comment says the argparse default "faked the gate rather than excluding it" -- but that repair lived in the CALLER, so a launch path that did not go through the arms table got the substituted suite back. **7 of 7 prose runs in the archive passed no `--test-cmd` at all and carried the default**, Wilson [0.645670, 1.000000], Clopper-Pearson [0.590384, 1.000000], the earliest being `study_run1b_2026-10-03`. **THE REPAIR HAS 2 HALVES AND THEIR COMPOSITION IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED**, because `composability-requires-a-measurement` excludes the weak reading. (A) the baseline is measured in the same sandbox before the candidate is written, and a failure present without the candidate is no longer blamed on it; (B) the non-Python refusal is hoisted above the command check. Named property: the number of 4 candidate classes receiving a verdict TRUE of the candidate. **Composed 4 of 4, against 2 of 4 for (A) alone, 3 of 4 for (B) alone and 1 of 4 before the repair**, so the pair dominates either half and neither is redundant. **GREEN-ONLY PROMOTION IS NOT LOOSENED.** The C0001 lesson is that the run-time S_k score tolerates regressions and so the gate must not; a candidate introducing ANY new failing node-id is still rejected, and the anti-vacuity class -- a candidate shadowing the `ImmuneMemory` class the suite imports -- is refused by node-id name. Nor is the policy new: `bench/build_acceptance.py` settled it on 2026-08-22 and pinned it with `test_step_three_compares_against_the_parent_rather_than_assuming_green`. 2 mechanisms were doing 1 job and only one of them had the fix. Its parser is REUSED rather than rewritten, because `failing_nodeids` counts collection ERRORs alongside FAILEDs -- the 2026-08-23 lesson, where matching only FAILED returned an empty set for a patch that broke every test in the repository. **ITS OWN P-PASS FOUND A DEFECT IN THE FIRST VERSION.** A pytest collection error exits 2, and the first version refused every abnormal exit before comparing node-ids -- which would have reinstated the very fault being fixed wherever the sandbox already aborts without the candidate. The baseline now caches its exit code alongside its failure set. **A MEASUREMENT APPEARED TO REFUTE MY PREDICTION AND THE REFUTATION WAS MY OWN INSTRUMENT.** The composability script predicted that (A) alone would FALSELY ACCEPT prose. The first run showed it REJECTING prose for `ast:invalid syntax`, and that was written up as the prediction being half wrong. It was not: disabling the hoisted refusal by patching `is_python_target` also re-enabled the syntax branch for prose, which reproduces the pre-2026-10-17 defect rather than the half-fix under test. `_apply_back_gate` makes exactly 2 consultations of that predicate per call, always in the same order with the syntax branch first, verified by execution rather than by reading; the simulation now answers the first consultation truthfully and the second with True. **On the faithful simulation (A) alone ACCEPTS both prose candidates**, reporting `ok (no new failures; 3 pre-existing, baseline rc1)`, so the prediction held and a FALSE ACCEPT is what the missing half would cost -- worse than the false reject it replaces, and the strongest part of the case for keeping both. The lesson is the one in `feedback_a_correction_needs_checking_too_2026-10-11`: a withdrawal needs the same scrutiny as the claim it withdraws. **PRODUCERS AND GUARD.** `scripts/the_apply_back_gate_has_no_baseline_2026-11-02.py` for the defect, `scripts/the_apply_back_baseline_mutations_2026-11-02.py` for the 4 classes and the composability measurement, `bench/tests/test_the_apply_back_gate_has_a_baseline_2026-11-02.py` for the guard -- 13 tests in 0.91 s, which point `REPO_ROOT` at a 5-file tree and fake the suite so the board never pays for a 364 MiB copy, and which need no live defect to keep their force. `scripts/the_apply_back_baseline_guard_mutations_2026-11-02.py` reverts each half in turn: **5 of 5 mutations red**, subject restored byte-for-byte by sha256. **RECOMMENDATION, against the 3 formal standards.** ADDITIVE: no capability is removed, green-only is unchanged, and the facility gains the ability to promote for the first time in its recorded life. SIMPLEST SUFFICIENT: the baseline is measured where the gate already builds its sandbox, and the sibling's parser is imported rather than a second one written. COMPOSABILITY: satisfied in his sense, by the 4-of-4 against 3-of-4 measurement above and not by the observation that the halves coexist. **THE DECISION THIS LEAVES HIM, AND IT IS A NEW RISK THE REPAIR CREATES.** A gate that could never accept anything masked a second question: whether the configured suite can see the target at all. Now that promotion is reachable, a target the suite does not exercise would yield a FALSE ACCEPT, which is worse than the false reject it replaces. The run archive shows the exposure is real rather than theoretical, since 7 of 7 prose runs were handed a suite chosen by argparse rather than for the target. The project already has the instrument for this -- the discrimination control, which asks whether a check behaves differently when the target is replaced wholesale -- and it is the instrument a discrimination control would use. **NEEDS HIS RULING:** whether `_apply_back_gate` must prove its suite can see the target before promoting, at the cost of a 3rd suite run per candidate, or whether the launcher should instead refuse to substitute a default suite for a target whose run named no suite at all. The recommendation is the launcher-side fix, and doing BOTH is explicitly not recommended, because no measurement shows the composed form dominating either part alone. **B92. The note linter's future-stamp rule dated a bare clock from the file's mtime, and accused 16 notes of claiming a day none of them named.** Added 2026-11-03T00:19:29+00:00. **STATUS: FIXED, TESTED, MUTATION-TESTED, COMMITTED. Not a decision.** **FOUND BY THE RULE BLOCKING A COMMIT**, which is the second time in 2 days that a probe's own location manufactured the failure it reported. A reply file written at 23:38 on the 2nd of November, stamped "2 November 2026, 23:40 GMT", was reported as claiming `2026-11-03 23:40`, 23 hours in the future, because the pre-commit hook lints a temporary `after_<name>` copy whose mtime is the moment of the check, and the clock had passed midnight. **THE CAUSE.** `future_stamp` in `scripts/note_vagueness_lint.py` prefers an ISO stamp that `STAMP_LINE` can parse -- `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ZONE` at the start of a line -- and otherwise falls back to a bare clock time in the header which it dates FROM THE MTIME. That is correct only while a note is never touched again. **AND THE FALLBACK IS THE BRANCH THAT NORMALLY RUNS:** of the 639 notes in `experimental_notes/`, only **145** carry a stamp `STAMP_LINE` parses against **205** carrying a bare clock and 289 carrying neither, so the mtime-dated path handles **205 of 350, 0.585714, Wilson 95% [0.533449, 0.636118]**. **MEASURED FALSE-POSITIVE RATE: of the 53 notes the rule accused, 16 carried a prose date in the very same header that exonerates them -- 16 of 53, 0.301887, Wilson 95% [0.195183, 0.435368], Clopper-Pearson [0.183402, 0.443434].** `Divergence_Directive_Implementation_2026-04-15.md` says "15 April 2026, 22:40" and was accused of claiming 2026-07-28 22:40 because its mtime is the 28th of July; it never named July. **THE FIX IS ADDITIVE AND READS A FIELD THE RULE ALREADY HAD IN FRONT OF IT:** the fallback now uses a prose date from the same header with the bare clock, keeping mtime only when no prose date is present. The comparison against mtime is unchanged, so a genuine future stamp is still accused and the accusation now quotes the day the note actually names. Accusations fall from 53 to 37. **WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE BLOCKED COMMIT:** the standing lesson is that a false positive is how a report-only linter becomes ignored while a true positive hides behind it, and this rule is BLOCKING at commit time on a per-file worsening. **GUARD:** `bench/tests/test_a_bare_clock_is_dated_from_the_header_2026-11-03.py`, 7 tests, pinning both the new silence and the retained noise -- a same-day clock 2 hours ahead is still caught, a header dated tomorrow is still caught and the accusation must quote the header's day, an ISO stamp is still read in preference, and a header with a bare clock and NO date still falls back to mtime so that case is narrowed rather than dropped. **MUTATIONS:** `scripts/the_bare_clock_dating_mutations_2026-11-03.py`, **4 of 4 red**, linter restored byte-for-byte by sha256; M3 replaces the base with a fixed future epoch so the rule accuses nobody, which from outside is indistinguishable from the rule being switched off. **PRODUCER:** `scripts/a_bare_clock_was_dated_from_the_mtime_2026-11-03.py`. **9 pre-existing ruff findings in `note_vagueness_lint.py` were left alone and are flagged rather than fixed**, since they are unrelated to this repair and predate it at HEAD.

The 2 decisions left over from the verified-flag repair: what `v_bar` is supposed to measure, and what the 4 sibling runners should do about a close path with no execution behind it.** Added 2026-11-03T00:36:00+00:00. **STATUS: MEASURED. NEEDS HIS RULING: on both halves. Raised as its own entry DELIBERATELY.** **WHY IT IS SEPARATE FROM B91 RATHER THAN A PARAGRAPH INSIDE IT.** B91's repair is DONE and COMMITTED, so B91 carries `state: DONE`, and the morning report builds its decisions section from entries that are still OPEN. A decision recorded inside a closed entry is therefore invisible on the 1 surface that exists to show him decisions -- the same shape as the 4th instance of 2 surfaces reporting different numbers, and the reason the rule is "pin a set, not a count". Splitting them out is the fix. **DECISION 1: WHAT `v_bar` MEASURES, AND WHETHER THE PARSER SHOULD READ A MODEL'S OWN VERIFIED CLAIM AT ALL.** `bench/dm/_manager.py:717` computes `v_bar` as the fraction of a model's findings whose `verified` flag is true, and `bench/dm/_types.py:331` documents it as mean verification quality. It is 1 of the 4 dimensions of the CapabilityFingerprint, and `bench/dm/_role_assignment.py:81` scores a model as the dot product of a role's alpha vector with the normalised fingerprint, with `_tie_break_key` at `:85` placing `v_bar` second in a lexicographic order whose own docstring says higher values win. **So `v_bar` enters role assignment positively.** The flag it reads can be set either by an execution or by the model writing `"VERIFIED": true` in its own reply, and **nothing in the stored fingerprints records which setter produced a value**. The dimension is not inert -- **38 of 50 archived `v_bar` observations are nonzero, 0.760000, Wilson 95% [0.625873, 0.857026]** -- but because the setter is unrecorded, **no claim is made here that self-reporting has actually moved a role assignment**, and that boundary is deliberate rather than cautious phrasing. **THE QUESTION IS WHICH QUANTITY HE WANTS.** If `v_bar` is meant to measure how often a model's findings were VERIFIED BY THIS MACHINE, the parser should stop populating the flag from a model's reply and `v_bar` becomes a smaller, honest number. If it is meant to measure how often a model CLAIMS verification, it is measuring that correctly today and the name is wrong. **A third option exists and is the additive one:** keep both, as 2 fields, and let him choose which one the fingerprint reads. It was not taken unasked because changing what `v_bar` counts changes a measurement that drives the experiment. **DECISION 2: THE 4 SIBLING RUNNERS.** The same confirmed-to-closed gate reading the same flag sits at `bench/reference_runner.py:858`, `bench/run_exp35_policy_engine.py:678`, `bench/run_exp36_evidence.py:845` and `bench/run_exp37_evidence.py:851`. In all 4 the only setter of `verified` is `mark_verified`, and **none of the 4 writes `falsifier_verdict` or references `bugzilla_verified` anywhere**, so the precondition added to the canonical runner would make their close path unreachable instead of guarded -- disabling a feature, which the additive standard forbids. **This is the measured answer to his Q15 about folding fixes back: a tested fix does not always fold back.** v1 is not dead code -- 36 live files reference it by word boundary, `bench/immune_agents.py` and `bench/endocrine.py` among them. **THE MISLABEL IS NARROWER THAN THE DEFECT, which matters for how urgent this is:** v1 and its 3 siblings close with a bare `resolve(cid, "CLOSED", round_idx)` passing no adjudicator, so their closures are UNLABELLED rather than falsely attributed to a tool, which is why 840 of 1562 archived closures carry an empty `status_adjudicator`. The false `adjudicator="tool"` was v3 only and is fixed. **THE 3 OPTIONS FOR THE 4 SIBLINGS.** Give them an execution path, which means porting falsifier machinery into runners whose experiments have already completed. Or change their closure to record honestly what it rests on, which is a label change and not a behaviour change. Or leave them, on the ground that their experiments are finished and their archives are read rather than extended. **THE RECOMMENDATION, under the formal standards:** the label change, because it is the SIMPLEST SUFFICIENT change that removes the untruth without removing the feature, and because porting machinery into a completed experiment's runner adds a surface nothing will exercise, which the symmetric form of the additive standard treats as not additive. **A RATCHET IS ALREADY IN PLACE SO THIS CANNOT GO QUIET:** `bench/tests/test_a_models_word_does_not_close_a_finding_2026-11-03.py::TestWhyTheFixWasNotFoldedBack` fails if any of the 4 later gains a `falsifier_verdict` writer, at which point the fold-back becomes possible and the test says so. **AND THE SIZE OF THE EXPOSURE IS NOW DERIVED RATHER THAN LEFT AS 'NOT INERT'.** `_capability_score` is the dot product of a role's weight vector with the normalised fingerprint, and those weight vectors sum to 1 -- asserted, with NumPy and SymPy agreeing -- so the v_bar weight IS v_bar's share of the entire score. It is **0.350000 for PM, the orchestrator seat, 0.300000 for COL and 0.250000 for PAR**. `as_normalised_array` sets the term to `v_bar / pool_max`, so SymPy confirms symbolically that the maximum gain from inflating v_bar to the pool maximum is **exactly that weight**: `alpha1*v/m` at `v = m` minus the same at `v = 0` simplifies to `alpha1`. **AND IT IS WORSE THAN ADDITIVE, because the pool maximum is the DENOMINATOR.** A model that inflates its own v_bar BECOMES the pool maximum, so an honest model's term falls from 1.000000 to its own raw v_bar: an honest model at 0.800000 loses 0.070000 of the orchestrator score, 0.060000 of the classifier score and 0.050000 of the worker score. So normalising by the pool maximum both raises the self-reporter and depresses everyone else. **THIS IS DERIVED, NOT MEASURED, and the distinction is load-bearing:** it follows from the equations and says nothing about whether it has happened. Nothing in the stored fingerprints records which setter produced a v_bar, so no archived role assignment can be attributed to self-reporting, and none is. Producer: `scripts/what_a_self_reported_v_bar_is_worth_2026-11-03.py`.

It was closed as though both were.
